title: 3 משחקי קופסא שיעזרו להם לשתף פעולה ביחד

stage.need: Playing together toward one shared goal and following the rules of a game with other children. CDC lists 'Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children' at 5 years and says playing with others helps children learn the value of sharing and friendship. Cooperative games (everyone wins or loses together) give that practice a concrete form.
stage.age_caveat: Milestones describe what most children do by an age, not a deadline. Some 5 year olds play together easily and some need more time; the caption says יש ילדים ש... and the games are labelled by their official age.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children / Teach your child to follow rules in games. For example, play simple board games, card games, or Simon Says. / Let your child play with other children, such as at a park or library. Playing with others helps your child learn the value of sharing and friendship.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year social milestone (follows rules or takes turns in games with other children) and the tips to play simple board games and to play with others, which helps learn sharing and friendship. Read today through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); the three sentences are quoted as returned, joined with ' / '.

dev_sources.title: Playing a cooperative game promotes preschoolers' sharing with third-parties, but not social inclusion
dev_sources.publisher: Toppe, Hardecker & Haun, PLoS One 2019 (PubMed Central, NIH)
dev_sources.quote: Dyads of 4- to 5-year-old children (N = 96) played the same game cooperatively, competitively, or solitarily. / Children shared less with third-parties after playing the game competitively than after playing it cooperatively.
dev_sources.supports: Peer reviewed, 4 to 5 year olds: after a cooperative game children shared more with an uninvolved peer than after a competitive one. Limit: the same study found no difference in social inclusion or free play, so the slides only say practise, never that games build cooperation.

products.popularity_reasoning: No strong signal (108th of 465 at Toys R Us is supporting). Two independent supporting signals from different groups: several Israeli retailers stock it, and an established Israeli publisher issues the Hebrew edition. Meets the rule only through the two-signal route, so the label is the weaker kind of popular_in_israel.
products.developmental_relevance: A fully cooperative race: all players move the owls home before sunrise and win or lose together, and on each turn a player may choose the card that helps whoever plays next. That gives young children a concrete rule for helping each other toward one goal.
products.parent_tip_source: Our suggestion, grounded in the publisher's rules page which says that in a cooperative game one player can decide to help the player who plays after them: before each turn the children ask 'איזה כרטיס יעזור לכולם?'.

claims.wording_he: משחקי קופסא שיעזרו להם לשתף פעולה ביחד
claims.supports: CDC 5 years: teach children to follow rules in games, for example simple board games, and playing with others helps them learn the value of sharing and friendship; PLoS One 2019 (4 to 5 year olds): children shared more with a peer after a cooperative game than after a competitive one. 'Can help' only; the same study found no effect on social inclusion.

claims.wording_he: בגיל 5 הרבה ילדים כבר משחקים ביחד לפי חוקים
claims.supports: CDC 5 year milestone: follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children.

claims.wording_he: משחקים שכולם בהם באותה קבוצה מאפשרים להם לתרגל לעזור אחד לשני
claims.supports: Cooperative games (all players on one team, win or lose together) are the format the PLoS One study compared to competitive play; CDC: playing with others helps children learn sharing and friendship. Written as an opportunity to practise, not a result.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים לעזור אחד לשני כשכולם מנצחים או מפסידים ביחד
claims.supports: Fox Mind's rules page: in a cooperative game all players work together toward one goal, win or loss shared. Practising helping each other follows CDC (playing with others) and the PLoS One cooperative-game study.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים להחליט ביחד אם מחפשים חשודים או חושפים רמזים
claims.supports: Fox Mind's Outfoxed rules: each turn the team decides whether to search for suspects or reveal clues, one shared goal. The practice of deciding together is our reading of cooperative play, sourced by CDC (play with others) and the PLoS One study.

claims.wording_he: סיפור מותאם אישית עם תמונות של הילדים שלכם
claims.supports: Live site, 2026-10-11: the order flow asks to upload the child's photo and add the name; the child is the hero.

claims.wording_he: שבו הם מגלים שהצלחה ביחד מתוקה מכל ממתק
claims.supports: Catalogue book 21 (lumebook.com, 2026-10-11): shared achievements are sweeter than any candy; learns the value of cooperation and true friendship.

notes: Games research 2026-10-11 (22:15 to 23:00): Toys R Us Israel best-selling sort read page by page (ranks 1 to 360 counted by hand; page 10 of 12 failed to load so ranks beyond 360 were not used). Skill chosen: cooperation, ages 5 to 6 (blocked skills avoided, 6-7 avoided). First idea was memory (CDC 5y and Harvard 5-7 support it) but no catalogue book fits memory and the games found there were weak or out of stock, so it was dropped. Rejected: חלומות 2 (Fox Mind, cooperative but 8+), מפלצות (Kodkod, out of stock at Toys R Us), Stitch memory (licensed, age unclear). The two games are from the same maker (Fox Mind), a reviewer warning, because the Israeli cooperative games for 4 to 6 are almost all Fox Mind. Both are popular_in_israel only through two supporting signals. Kodkod site returned a firewall block, so no Kodkod pages were used. CDC pages were read through a page fetch because curl is blocked.
